# Alan Review Tool

> A Manifest V3 browser extension (Chrome and Firefox) for capturing UI/UX
> feedback on any website - text comments and screenshots, organized into a
> session, exported as a self-contained HTML report.

No backend, no bundler, no site-side integration required - a reviewer
clicks the toolbar icon on any tab and a slide-out panel appears.

## Reference documentation

- [README](README.md): What this is, how to build it, how to load it in
  Chrome/Firefox, and the local development scripts.
- [ARCHITECTURE](ARCHITECTURE.md): Injection/lifecycle model, the storage
  data model, the report format, the build's file-inlining mechanism, and
  the migration discipline required for any data-shape change.
- [AGENTS](AGENTS.md): Rules for AI agents making changes to this codebase -
  read this and ARCHITECTURE.md before planning a change.

## Layout

- `src/manifest.chrome.json`, `src/manifest.firefox.json` - Per-browser MV3
  manifests. Differ only in their `background` block.
- `src/background.js` - Service worker: injects `content.js` on toolbar
  click, captures screenshots on request from the content script.
- `src/content.js` - The entire panel: rendering, session/comment state,
  screenshot capture and cyan-annotation lightbox, and the downloaded
  report's HTML generation. Re-injected fresh on every toolbar click.
- `src/content.css` - Styles the live panel (loaded via `<link>` inside its
  shadow root).
- `src/report.css` - Styles the downloaded report only. Inlined into
  `content.js` at build time, not loaded at runtime.
- `src/ai-report-instructions.txt` - Hidden, AI-readable instructions
  explaining the report's structure, also inlined into `content.js` at
  build time.
- `build.js` - Copies the shared files into `dist/chrome` and
  `dist/firefox`, pairs each with its own manifest, and performs the
  report.css/ai-report-instructions.txt inlining step.
- `dist/` - Build output (git-ignored). Load `dist/chrome` or
  `dist/firefox` as an unpacked/temporary extension to run it.
- `.changeset/` - Changesets config; this package is private and never
  published to npm, so versioning/changelog tracking is the point, not a
  registry publish.
- `.github/workflows/` - `pull-request.yml` (lint + build on every PR) and
  `release.yml` (Changesets' Version-Packages-PR flow).
